guide_enrichment.narrative:
We understand why Miami’s early dominance has pushed this price so high. Miami followed its opening win with a 77-7 rout of Florida A&M, setting a program record with 856 total yards while allowing only 107. Those results matter, but we are not treating one overwhelming performance as the baseline for every future margin. For us, the case is less about expecting Central Michigan to match Miami and more about resisting the market’s aggressive extrapolation of that blowout.

Our biggest concern is Central Michigan’s ability to generate scoring opportunities against a Miami defense that grades among the nation’s best in preventing them. The underlying rushing and passing matchups are less extreme, however, which gives Central Michigan at least a path to moving the ball between the 20s. We do not need Central Michigan to control the game; we need it to do enough offensively to avoid the kind of possession-by-possession collapse that Miami forced against Florida A&M. That distinction is why our numbers support taking the points.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Central Michigan’s offense on money downs. Miami’s first two opponents converted only 21 percent of their third downs and failed on both fourth-down attempts, reinforcing what our scoring-opportunity metrics already show. If Central Michigan repeatedly gives the ball back before crossing midfield, Miami has the offensive firepower to create separation quickly. If it can extend a few drives and turn limited opportunities into points, the size of the cushion becomes much more meaningful.

recent_game.fact: Miami improved to 2-0 with a 77-7 home win over Florida A&M on Sept. 10, 2026.
Miami set a program record with 856 total yards and an ACC record with 42 first downs against Florida A&M; its 77 points tied the program record.
Miami rushed for 430 yards, passed for 426 yards and averaged 11.7 yards per play against Florida A&M.
Miami held Florida A&M's offense to 107 total yards, four first downs and 1-of-14 third-down conversions; Florida A&M's only touchdown came on a 72-yard fumble return.
Running back Javian Mallory rushed 10 times for 142 yards and two touchdowns against Florida A&M, including a 52-yard touchdown.
Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. rushed for 105 yards against Florida A&M.

quarterback.fact: Darian Mensah, a January transfer from Duke, has started both games for Miami in 2026.
Mensah completed 14 of 15 passes for 252 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions against Florida A&M.
Through two games, Mensah has completed 41 of 45 passes for 653 yards, eight touchdowns and no interceptions.
Backup quarterback Luke Nickel completed all eight of his passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns against Florida A&M in his first major college action.
Mensah, Nickel and Dereon Coleman combined for six touchdown passes and only two incompletions against Florida A&M.

offensive_personnel.fact: Miami used the same five offensive-line starters in its first two games: Samson Okunlola at left tackle, SJ Alofaituli at left guard, Ryan Rodriguez at center, Max Buchanan at right guard and Matthew McCoy at right tackle.
Four of Miami's five 2025 offensive-line starters departed for the NFL, including drafted tackles Francis Mauigoa and Markel Bell and guard Anez Cooper.
Wide receiver Cooper Barkate transferred from Duke after catching 72 passes for 1,106 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025; he previously played three seasons at Harvard.
Barkate and Mensah were teammates at Duke in 2025 before both transferred to Miami.
Wide receiver Malachi Toney had four receptions for 96 yards and one touchdown against Florida A&M after setting a Miami single-game record with 234 receiving yards and three touchdowns at Stanford.
Miami returned its top six rushers from 2025 and 97.9 percent of its rushing production.

defensive_personnel.fact: Miami lost 2025 starting edge defenders Rueben Bain Jr. and Akheem Mesidor to the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft.
Defensive tackles Ahmad Moten Sr. and Justin Scott, both starters in the 2025 national championship game, returned for 2026 and started Miami's first two games.
Miami added edge defender Damon Wilson II from Missouri after he recorded nine sacks and earned second-team All-SEC honors in 2025.
Linebacker Mohamed Toure started all 16 games in 2025 and led Miami with 84 tackles.
Defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald recorded six interceptions in 2025, leading Miami and the ACC and tying for the Power Four lead.

Miami changed four defensive starters between its first two games: Kamal Bonner, JJ Dunnigan and Damari Brown entered the lineup against Florida A&M, while Bryce Fitzgerald moved from safety to cornerback.

injury_availability.fact: Defensive tackle Ahmad Moten Sr. missed spring practice while recovering from an injury sustained in 2025, but he started Miami's first two games of 2026.

offensive_context.fact: Through two games, Miami averaged 61.0 points, 702.5 total yards, 427.0 passing yards and 275.5 rushing yards per game.
Miami averaged 10.0 yards per play and converted 64 percent of its third downs through two games.
Miami scored touchdowns on 8 of its first 10 red-zone opportunities in 2026.
Miami scored on 11 of its first 12 possessions against Florida A&M.

defensive_context.fact: Miami allowed 6.5 points, 57.5 rushing yards and 145.5 passing yards per game through its first two contests.
Miami's first two opponents converted 21 percent of their third downs and failed on both fourth-down attempts.
In defensive coordinator Corey Hetherman's first season in 2025, Miami ranked first in the ACC in total defense, scoring defense and rushing defense.
Miami recorded three sacks through its first two games of 2026.

special_teams.fact: Jake Weinberg handled Miami's primary kicking duties in the opener and made a 46-yard field goal against Stanford.

Miami entered the Wake Forest week 2-0 after wins of 45-6 at Stanford and 77-7 over Florida A&M.
